sketches.mechanism: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance, forever alone, impossible to duplicate
sketches.resonance: Declaring yourself as an object means the language guarantees there will only ever be one of you, and no one can make another.

sketches.mechanism: method_missing is invoked whenever you call a method that doesn't exist — the object gets to decide how to respond to things it was never taught
sketches.resonance: A parent who responds to every question they were never prepared for, always returning the child's own name back to them.
sketches.draft:
class Parent
  def method_missing(question, *_)
    question
  end

  def respond_to_missing?(*)
    true
  end
end

sketches.mechanism: A value moved into a closure cannot be accessed afterward — the original binding becomes permanently invalid after the closure captures it
sketches.resonance: Giving yourself to something means the version of you that existed before is gone; the compiler enforces that you cannot go back.
